question: Which Indian-origin author's debut novel, We Need New Names, was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize in 2013?
solution:
The correct answer is __**NoViolet Bulawayo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NoViolet Bulawayo** is the author of the debut novel **"We Need New Names."**
 
• The book was shortlisted for the prestigious **Man Booker Prize** in **2013**, making it a significant achievement in contemporary literature.
 
• NoViolet Bulawayo is a Zimbabwean author, and her real name is **Elizabeth Zandile Tshele**. She adopted the pen name "NoViolet" as a tribute to her late mother.
 
• **"We Need New Names"** is a coming-of-age story that explores the challenges faced by a young girl named Darling as she grows up in a politically and economically unstable Zimbabwe.
 
• The novel provides powerful insights into themes of **identity, migration, and displacement**, which resonated with a global audience, earning it critical acclaim and recognition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Man Booker Prize:**

 
 
• The **Man Booker Prize** is one of the most prestigious literary awards in the world, awarded annually for the best original novel written in the English language.
 
• It was established in **1969** and is open to writers of any nationality, provided their work is published in the UK or Ireland.
 
• The prize aims to promote high-quality fiction and recognizes authors for their outstanding literary contributions.
 
 
 
• **Key Themes in "We Need New Names":**
 
 
• The novel delves into the struggles of **adolescence** and the longing for a better life in the face of adversity.
 
• It highlights the impact of political turmoil and economic instability on ordinary lives in Zimbabwe.
 
• The book also explores the experiences of **immigrants** in Western countries and the sense of alienation and loss of cultural roots.
 
 
 
• **About NoViolet Bulawayo:**
 
 
• NoViolet Bulawayo was born on **31 October 1981**, in Zimbabwe.
 
• She studied at **Texas A&M University** and later obtained her MFA in Creative Writing from **Cornell University**.
 
• Her work often reflects themes of political activism, cultural identity, and social justice.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Chigozie Obioma**: A Nigerian author known for his debut novel **"The Fishermen"**, which was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize in **2015**.
 
• **Aravind Adiga**: An Indian author who won the **Man Booker Prize in 2008** for his debut novel **"The White Tiger."**
 
• **Jhumpa Lahiri**: An Indian-American author awarded the **Pulitzer Prize for Fiction** in **2000** for her debut short story collection **"Interpreter of Maladies."**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• NoViolet Bulawayo is the first **black African woman** to be shortlisted for the **Man Booker Prize**, a milestone in literary history.
 
• The novel **"We Need New Names"** has been translated into several languages, reflecting its global appeal and relevance.
 
• The book is studied in academic institutions worldwide for its portrayal of post-colonial struggles and immigrant experiences.
 
• NoViolet Bulawayo continues to be a prominent voice in contemporary literature, with her works addressing critical social and political issues.
